definition: A forward is an OTC contract for future delivery, typically unmargined with no cash flows until the delivery date, usually a direct bilateral agreement under an ISDA master agreement. A future is an exchange-traded contract for future delivery that is freely tradable and requires daily mark-to-market profit/loss to be settled via margin payments.
core_idea: Forwards and futures both fix a future delivery, but differ in venue (OTC vs. exchange), tradability, and cash-flow timing (settlement-date-only vs. daily margin).
key_points: Forwards: OTC, typically not margined, no cash flow until delivery.
Futures: exchange-traded, freely tradable, daily mark-to-market margin settlement required.
relationships: Ties to Exchange vs OTC Trading and Margin/Mark-to-Market definitions.
trading_implications: Futures' daily margin settlement means P&L is realized incrementally in cash, while a forward's P&L is only realized at delivery — this affects funding/liquidity needs during the life of the position.
